analysis:
Scope: StandaloneServer.swift ensureModelLoaded. Base lines 1964-1971 and 2001-2004 are the only changed regions. The supplied head text covers only lines 1-586 (headers, config, init, setModels), and the patch excerpt is truncated in the post-load hunk, so the new head load path (~1964-2010) is not visible. The visible head text has no security-relevant change.

Patch behaviour. For managed GLM loads (glmPlan != nil), the pre-load computeStandaloneWeightHash is now invoked with required: artifactIdentityRequired && glmPlan == nil. The explicit pre-load check against glmPlan.weights.manifest.aggregateSHA256 (base 1966-1969) is removed. Only glmPlan.weights.recheck() remains. The post-load hash comparison and the identityMismatch throw (base 2003-2005) are replaced by code I cannot see. A code comment says the managed GLM load SHA-256-verifies every manifest file and that this verified digest replaces both bracketing passes.

Relevant threats: T-012, T-027 (weight substitution), T-041 (reusable SSD cache keyed on cacheEligibleWeightHash/modelArtifactSHA256, whose binding is a detection_hint item), and T-050/TB-007 context.

Unverified contracts the next pass must check:
1. GLM5NextManagedLoad.adopting and the loader actually hash every manifest file, reading the same bytes that MLX loads. This must close the TOCTOU gap that the pre-load and post-load bracket used to cover, and operator replacement of files during load must still fail closed.
2. The post-load identity (head ~1999-2006) is derived from that verified digest and still equals manifest.aggregateSHA256. A nil or unverified value must throw rather than flow into reusableSSDWeightHashDecision.
3. With preLoadArtifactHash nil for GLM, ProviderLoop.reusableSSDWeightHashDecision must not yield .eligible with an unverified hash. It should yield .unavailable, or the head must substitute the verified digest, so the SSD cache binding in T-041 and the modelArtifactSHA256 qualification are not weakened.
4. The glmPlan.weights.recheck() ordering relative to the load.

No concrete regression is demonstrable from the visible evidence. Because the identity-check replacement is hidden, this remains uncertain and affects a security conclusion.
